fact: MTN MoMo, a mobile money service, trained 1,225 South Sudanese entrepreneurs to accept digital payments, sell airtime and provide cash-in services, per Tech Africa News.

MTN MoMo mobile money is in service in South Sudan, letting users send and receive money, pay bills and shop by phone, as MTN launched its 'Mata fekir' campaign with the Bank of South Sudan governor present, per One Citizen Daily.
One Citizen Daily calls MTN and Digitel two of South Sudan's leading mobile money operators, and MTN MoMo urges traders and customers to use mobile money to buy goods and services.
Traders and buyers in Juba report using mobile money, citing network failures and high withdrawal costs, after the Bank of South Sudan directed sellers to accept it.
The Bank of South Sudan said mobile money is recognised as a legal form of payment under the Electronic Money Regulation 2017 and that providers and agents are operating.
The article describes rules for operating electronic money systems in South Sudan, with transaction limits by customer tier and agent reporting, implying mobile money services are in operation.
ITWeb Africa reports South Sudan MTN MoMo users can now receive money from 15 countries, so the MTN mobile money service is in service.
The report says South Sudan's cash crisis has affected mobile money transfer service providers as well as banks.
